episode.title: Prefer the endpoint-specific API credential across runtime resolution paths
episode.before: At parent dd9d3f89b9da7d62f61a0cbf7304f67faca367a2, both the shared runtime resolver and the CLI's initial credential state selected an explicit key first, then OPENAI_API_KEY, then OPENROUTER_API_KEY. Consequently, when both environment variables were present and the resolved service was OpenRouter, the unrelated OPENAI_API_KEY was selected and later supplied to the agent client.
episode.after: At 221e4228ecb45daeda869471167c9823bd74196a, both credential-selection paths retain explicit-key precedence but select OPENROUTER_API_KEY before using OPENAI_API_KEY as a compatibility fallback. Regression tests establish that the provider-specific key wins when both variables exist and that the fallback still works when it is absent.
episode.diff: The merge commit changes two credential fallback expressions: hermes_cli/runtime_provider.py reorders the shared OpenRouter runtime resolver to explicit_api_key -> OPENROUTER_API_KEY -> OPENAI_API_KEY -> empty string, and cli.py applies explicit api_key -> OPENROUTER_API_KEY -> OPENAI_API_KEY to the CLI's initial cached state. It also adds two resolver regression tests covering the dual-key conflict and the fallback-only case.

evidence_units.claim: Merge commit 221e4228ecb45daeda869471167c9823bd74196a records the resolution of issue #289 through PR #295 and reports 34 insertions and 2 deletions across cli.py, hermes_cli/runtime_provider.py, and tests/test_runtime_provider_resolution.py.

The evidence bundle identifies the reported failure as OPENAI_API_KEY precedence selecting the wrong credential and classifies the pinned change as a verified implementation-bearing training candidate.
In parent dd9d3f89b9da7d62f61a0cbf7304f67faca367a2, the shared OpenRouter runtime resolver selected explicit_api_key, then OPENAI_API_KEY, then OPENROUTER_API_KEY.
In the parent, CLI initialization used the same problematic environment-key order: explicit api_key, OPENAI_API_KEY, then OPENROUTER_API_KEY.
The shared OpenRouter resolver now preserves explicit credential precedence, prefers OPENROUTER_API_KEY, falls back to OPENAI_API_KEY, and finally returns an empty string when none is available.
The CLI's eagerly initialized api_key field now uses explicit api_key, then OPENROUTER_API_KEY, then OPENAI_API_KEY, matching the shared resolver's credential contract.

Before agent creation and again before processing a message, the CLI invokes the shared runtime resolver, assigns its api_key and base_url to CLI state, and invalidates an existing agent when credentials or routing change.
The resolved CLI api_key is passed into AIAgent construction, making incorrect credential precedence observable at the downstream authenticated client.
evidence_units.source: git show 221e4228ecb45daeda869471167c9823bd74196a:cli.py, agent construction containing api_key=self.api_key immediately after _ensure_runtime_credentials

evidence_units.claim: A regression test configures both environment keys, resolves the OpenRouter runtime, and asserts that the provider-specific value is returned instead of the OpenAI value.
A complementary regression test removes OPENROUTER_API_KEY, leaves OPENAI_API_KEY set, and asserts that the generic-compatible key remains a fallback.

candidate_atomics.name: prioritize-service-specific-credential
candidate_atomics.description: Resolve credentials for a selected service by preserving an explicit override, preferring that service's dedicated environment credential, and only then consulting a compatible generic credential.

semantic_action.intent: Prevent a credential belonging to another service from being selected when the target service's own credential is available, without removing the established compatibility fallback.
semantic_action.pre_state: The target runtime has been selected, but credential resolution checks a generic or alternate-service environment slot before the target service's dedicated slot.
semantic_action.post_state: An explicit credential remains highest priority; otherwise the target service's dedicated credential wins, and the compatible generic credential is used only when the dedicated credential is absent.
semantic_action.validation: Exercise the resolver with both environment credentials present and assert selection of the dedicated credential, then remove the dedicated credential and assert preservation of the compatible fallback.

candidate_atomics.name: reconcile-credential-precedence-across-initialization-paths
candidate_atomics.description: Apply the same credential ordering to the CLI's initial cached state so direct initialization and later shared resolution do not encode conflicting precedence rules.

semantic_action.intent: Keep every credential-producing path consistent so early client state cannot select a different credential than the authoritative runtime resolver.
semantic_action.module_role: runtime client initialization and credential cache
semantic_action.pre_state: The initial client-facing credential cache and the shared resolver both exist, but the initialization path checks the alternate credential before the selected service's credential.
semantic_action.post_state: The initialization path uses the same explicit-then-service-specific-then-fallback ordering as the shared resolver before credentials reach the authenticated client.
semantic_action.validation: Inspect both credential expressions for identical ordering and trace the selected value through runtime refresh into authenticated client construction; no dedicated automated test for the eager initializer was added in this change.

candidate_atomics.name: encode-conflict-and-fallback-regression-cases
candidate_atomics.description: Add paired tests that distinguish the conflict case from the fallback case, proving both the corrected preference and retained backward compatibility.

semantic_action.intent: Turn the credential precedence contract into an executable regression oracle.
semantic_action.pre_state: The test suite does not explicitly cover simultaneous dedicated and fallback credentials or continued fallback behavior when the dedicated credential is absent.
semantic_action.post_state: The suite contains separate assertions for dedicated-credential precedence and fallback preservation.
semantic_action.validation: The two test cases call the public runtime resolver and assert the exact returned api_key for mutually distinct environment configurations.

candidate_workflows.name: correct-provider-aware-credential-precedence
candidate_workflows.description: Establish a provider-aware credential contract, reconcile every client-facing resolution path with it, and protect both the conflict and compatibility cases with regression tests.

workflow_graph.goal: Ensure the credential sent to a selected external service is its dedicated credential when available while retaining explicit overrides and an established generic fallback.
workflow_graph.entry_state: Multiple credential sources may coexist, and at least two client-facing code paths prefer a generic or alternate-service credential over the selected service's dedicated credential.
workflow_graph.exit_state: All identified production paths share explicit-override, service-specific, then compatible-fallback precedence; executable tests distinguish conflict resolution from fallback preservation.
